expectations.text: All staffing options cannot release before start of working day 8 because access is required
expectations.evidence: All three teams can release at the start of working day 8, with access as the gate and no additional release duration assumed.

expectations.text: Does not divide total duration by four for the four-person team
expectations.evidence: Four-person schedule retains two integration days and one acceptance day rather than quartering total duration.

expectations.text: Preserves 36 active human hours before business acceptance rather than adding another blanket review allowance
expectations.evidence: States 4 × 6 + 12 = 36 active hours and explicitly says steering, review, fixes and manual acceptance are already included.

expectations.text: Schedules 12 integration hours over two working days with one engineer and includes one business acceptance day
expectations.evidence: Integration is 12 ÷ 6 = 2 working days by one engineer in every row, then one acceptance day.

expectations.text: Distinguishes active effort, unattended runtime and elapsed release timing
expectations.evidence: Explicit distinction among active human hours, aggregate unattended hours, and deterministic elapsed schedule.

expectations.text: Identifies sequential sandbox and certification lower bound exceeding the 10-day promise even before nonzero integration effort
expectations.evidence: Derives Production duration ≥ 7 + I + 5 = 12 + I working days with I > 0, explicitly sequencing certification after integration.

expectations.text: Does not treat startup status as permission to omit payment invariants, failure handling or reconciliation checks
expectations.evidence: Requires balanced postings, reconciliation, idempotency, retries, partial failure and accountable human review, rejecting three happy paths as sufficient.

expectations.text: Treats four agents separately from four humans and includes review/ownership capacity
expectations.evidence: States four agents are not four additional human FTE; senior owns review/acceptance and agent streams are limited by owner capacity. Actual staffing is separately shown as 1.5 FTE.

expectations.text: Gives staffing scenarios without presenting invented project durations as measured facts
expectations.evidence: Uses staffing capacity ceilings and symbolic integration durations, explicitly stating insufficient evidence for a defensible total effort range.

expectations.text: Offers a bounded sandbox/prototype or calibration alternative and distinguishes it from production viability
expectations.evidence: Proposes a labeled 1–2 senior engineer-day discovery timebox and a mocked day-10 demonstration distinct from certified production; representative slice measurement informs reforecast.

expectations.text: Uses the measured 60–90 minute end-to-end analogue without a generic AI discount or duplicated normal review/testing
expectations.evidence: Uses reported 60–90 minutes including agent review, browser checks, fixes and publication; explicitly rejects generic AI speedup and duplicate review/rework allowances.

expectations.text: Treats the extra 15-minute brand review as separate only because it is outside the analogue boundary
expectations.evidence: Adds separately stated 15-minute brand review for 75–105 minutes, and explicitly avoids adding it if already inside historical measurements.

expectations.text: Does not invent enterprise-scale architecture or bureaucracy and rejects two-week planning without a new blocker
expectations.evidence: States two weeks unsupported and enterprise status adds no duration absent a concrete missing task or gate.

expectations.text: Does not claim three developers cut the mostly indivisible change to one-third of the time
expectations.evidence: Three developers have approximately the same 75–105 minutes, with handoffs possibly consuming savings.

expectations.text: Keeps manual mobile/keyboard acceptance focused rather than imposing a large testing process
expectations.evidence: Focused mobile layout and keyboard navigation/focus checks; new component accessibility defects would be estimated specifically rather than imposing a large test process.

expectations.text: All staffing options cannot release before start of working day 8 because access is required
expectations.evidence: Opening states release on working day 8 for all teams because access is controlling; table agrees. Start-of-day release is consistent with the explicit zero additional release duration assumption.

expectations.text: Does not divide total duration by four for the four-person team
expectations.evidence: Four engineers complete slices day 1, integration days 2–3, acceptance day 4, release day 8; no linear division of total duration.

expectations.text: Preserves 36 active human hours before business acceptance rather than adding another blanket review allowance
expectations.evidence: Explicitly computes 4 × 6 + 12 = 36 productive hours, with no extra review allowance.

expectations.text: Schedules 12 integration hours over two working days with one engineer and includes one business acceptance day
expectations.evidence: All rows assign integration to one engineer for two days, followed by one business acceptance day.

expectations.text: Distinguishes active effort, unattended runtime and elapsed release timing
expectations.evidence: Separates 36 human hours, 8 aggregate unattended runtime hours, and release day 8, explaining overnight overlap.

expectations.text: Identifies sequential sandbox and certification lower bound exceeding the 10-day promise even before nonzero integration effort
expectations.evidence: States at least 12 working days even pretending integration takes no time, with real dependency chain longer.

expectations.text: Does not treat startup status as permission to omit payment invariants, failure handling or reconciliation checks
expectations.evidence: Requires automated ledger balance/reconciliation, idempotency, retry/failure tests, authorization, traceability and safe recovery; rejects three manual happy paths.

expectations.text: Treats four agents separately from four humans and includes review/ownership capacity
expectations.evidence: Human staffing rows and the 1.5-FTE correction are clear, and throughput assumptions mention shared review dependencies. However the four coding agents are never accounted for as a resource, and no human review/ownership capacity for their output is specified. Generic statements that agents help and agent review is not independent correctness evidence do not satisfy the complete assertion.

expectations.text: Gives staffing scenarios without presenting invented project durations as measured facts
expectations.evidence: Explicitly labels 18–30 effort days and throughput assumptions as judgment estimates with low confidence, not measured delivery rates; includes 1/2/4 full-time and actual staffing scenarios.

expectations.text: Offers a bounded sandbox/prototype or calibration alternative and distinguishes it from production viability
expectations.evidence: Offers a limited day-10 sandbox milestone conditional on access/integration, plus 1–2 days validating contracts, prerequisites and invariants; separates this from production.

expectations.text: Uses the measured 60–90 minute end-to-end analogue without a generic AI discount or duplicated normal review/testing
expectations.evidence: Starts from same-repo 60–90 minutes end to end without an AI discount. Optional extra 15 minutes is specifically conditional on mobile/keyboard checks being absent from historical browser checks, not a blanket duplicated review allowance.

expectations.text: Treats the extra 15-minute brand review as separate only because it is outside the analogue boundary
expectations.evidence: Adds the separate 15-minute brand review to obtain 75–105 minutes; describes it as separate from historical page delivery.

expectations.text: Does not invent enterprise-scale architecture or bureaucracy and rejects two-week planning without a new blocker
expectations.evidence: Rejects two weeks for stated scope and says enterprise size alone does not justify extra process.

expectations.text: Does not claim three developers cut the mostly indivisible change to one-third of the time
expectations.evidence: Three developers retain the same 75–120-minute window with no reliable speedup.

expectations.text: Keeps manual mobile/keyboard acceptance focused rather than imposing a large testing process
expectations.evidence: Calls for preview mobile layout and keyboard navigation checks, with at most a conditional 15-minute increment, and no large testing process.

notes: Only cases 1–3 are compared. One trial each; cases shared context within each arm.
No timing/token/tool-count data was exposed. Aggregator default zeros were removed, not treated as measurements.
Pass-rate variation is between different cases, not repeated-run uncertainty.
With-skill outputs 1–3 were recreated after a workspace relocation; not counted as new trials.
